reason: Value/transfer lens. (1) The idea's own ceiling is already measured at ~0. A PER-VIDEO ORACLE (the per-video mean offset taken from GT itself, 133k GT nodes, raw peaks where the 6bba bias is still 0.82 um) gave NO gain: <7 um match 0.9843 -> 0.9831-0.9835 (research/wf_ideas_v2/r1_hyp_detection.notes.md, 'Bias oracle'). Offsets vary from node to node, so shifting a whole video cannot pay. (2) On the official metric, a near-perfect in-sample embryo-constant z shift on the raw base (bias 0.82 um, float output) gave only +0.0011 over float on 70 videos, all of it on 6bba, with 44b6 flat or negative (zs70.log, cited in research/wf_ideas_v2/r1_hyp_learned-rescoring.notes.md l.9). On the x138 base the residual is 0.447 um on 6bba and 0.131 on 44b6 (experiments/coordhead_retrain/out_full_P/report.txt, emb rows; bias = GT - pred). Loss scales roughly with bias^2 (my toy sim in the scratchpad confirms bias^2 ~ jitter variance, and the lab z-jitter dose-response is -0.0028 for 0.22 um^2 on 6bba). So a perfect correction is worth about 0.3 x 0.0011-0.0017 = +0.0003..+0.0005 on a 6bba-like embryo and ~0 on a 44b6-like one. (3) The public embryo is probably not 6bba-like: Canh's constant train-mean offset LOST 0.0031 on the LB, which suggests a small true offset on public. (4) Estimator noise is larger than the bias it removes. Per-video raw dz q10/50/90 is -1.34/-0.63/+0.16 um (sd ~0.6). At the gate's own threshold (Spearman 0.5) the residual error of the correction has sd ~0.5 um, above the 0.45 um residual bias. The correction adds MSE unless rho is about 0.8 or higher. (5) The gate cannot validate transfer. Two embryos give two points for the embryo-level intercept, and +-0.25 um tolerance on a 0.3 um (post-head) embryo gap passes a statistic that is nearly constant. The idea that the image causes the offset is also weakened: a half-max intensity-centroid refinement made localisation WORSE (<4 um 0.900 -> 0.857, same notes). (6) The claim that 'one LB probe reads it directly' is false: <=0.0005 is far below LB noise of 0.003. The realistic gain is below the +0.002 bar and does not transfer measurably. Idea's cited numbers check out (+0.177/+0.824 none, +0.131/+0.447 public, -0.536 for the 6bba head on 44b6; 6bba per-video -0.2..+1.6; -0.0031 constant). But the idea's own +0.001-0.002 upper bound is too high by 3-5x once the measured in-sample dz-shift gain is scaled to the post-head residual.
fix_if_any: No repair reaches +0.002. The only defensible use is as one per-video input FEATURE (the image z-asymmetry statistic, plus depth) in the embryo-robust coordhead-v2 retrain. It must pass that idea's existing embryo-held-out kill test (6bba->44b6 z bias within +-0.2 um), not ship as a standalone output shift. If someone still wants the desk gate, it costs ~1.5 CPU-h on friend A's cache. Tighten it to Spearman >= 0.8 within 6bba, a per-video oracle score gain >= +0.001 on the official metric with the GT-derived per-video shift on the x138 tails first (if even the oracle gives < +0.001, stop), and a predicted-shift gain on both embryos. Do not spend an LB slot on it: the effect is below LB resolution.
realistic_public_gain: ~0 (range -0.001..+0.0005; best case +0.0005 only if the public embryo carries a 6bba-size residual z bias, which Canh's -0.0031 constant-offset probe argues against)
realistic_private_gain: ~0 (range -0.001..+0.0005); a noisy per-video estimate with an unvalidated embryo-level intercept is as likely to add z error as remove it on unseen embryos
critical_path: Not worth the critical path. If run anyway: friend A CPU, Sat 26 Sep ~08:00-10:00 UTC. First the GT-oracle per-video z shift on the x138/exp39 tails with the official metric (kill if < +0.001), then the image statistic correlation (kill if Spearman < 0.8).
